name: 2017 Prairie Avenue: the brick stable on the alley, K12
aka: the stable behind the William Armour house, 2017 Prairie

grade.why: Known from maps or written records; no picture of it has been found.

documented_range.note: The draft's claim, kept: the 1911 sheet draws the building and the T-1842 census rules it present in 1904 (present_as_mapped). Nothing else read dates it, so the range claims the 1904 target and no more. TO is the last day of the year the sheet was published, the latest date anything here shows it standing; it is not a demolition date.

placement.position_note: The middle of the building's alley (east) wall at grade, read off the committed sheet 35 raster (chicago/reference/prairie-avenue/sanborn-1911-and-robinson-1886/sanborn_1911_vol3_sheet_35.jpg) at pixel (1170.96, 557.24): the alley line by a median darkness profile over rows 520-595 (peak at column 1170.96; the building's alley wall is drawn on it), halfway between the north wall line (row 516.27, a profile over columns 1120-1160) and the south wall line (row 598.21, the same columns), each peak refined by a parabola through the three highest samples. Carried to the local frame by the sheet's fitted similarity (data/traces/gcp/sanborn_1911_v3_sheet_35_gcps.json): local E 1469.966, N -3535.003. The bearing is the parcel's (prairie_2017, data/street_grid/1904.json, -0.611 degrees, the draft's 179.389 less the half turn its plan frame took). The fit's own residual, 0.05 m RMS on its control crossings, plus about a pixel (0.19 m) of reading on this coarse copy, is all that is claimed. The draft had stood its fitted 9.0 x 13.5 m rectangle from a corner 1.5 m east and 7.6 m north of this wall's middle, turned the other way.
placement.symbolic_location: 2017 S. Prairie Avenue, rear: east side of Prairie Avenue between 20th and 21st Streets, parcel prairie_2017 (data/street_grid/1904.json); on the rear lot line, its alley wall on the alley's west line, its north and south walls on the lot lines (Sanborn 1911 vol. 3 sheet 35).

footprint.note: About the middle of the alley wall, u east (toward the alley, so the building lies at negative u) and v north. The sheet draws the building from the alley line (pixel column 1170.96) back to its west wall line (column 1113.75, a profile over rows 525-590): 57.21 pixels at the sheet's 0.185854 m a pixel, 10.633 m; and from its north wall line (row 516.27) to its south wall line (row 598.21): 81.94 pixels, 15.229 m along the alley. A plain rectangle: the sheet draws no step, wing or porch on it. The lines 0.62 m north of the north wall (row 512.9) and 0.56 m south of the south wall (row 601) are 2013's and 2021's buildings, not this one's.

stories.note: '2' lettered in the building's north-east corner, under its north wall line. Built as the kit's carriage room (3.6 m) under a loft whose walls rise 2.7 m more to the eave, under a 40-degree roof (4.46 m from eave to ridge over the 10.63 m span); those heights are RECONSTRUCTED. No dormer: the sheet draws none and the kit builds none.

construction.note: Drawn pink, the sheet's colour for brick. The small figures written inside its north and south wall lines are too coarse on this copy to read as wall thicknesses; the kit builds its own 13-inch walls.

value.note: Everything but the plan, the two storeys, the brick and the window mark's place is RECONSTRUCTED from the K12 kit (L-k12-coach-house-kit-2320), recorded as L-k12-2017-stable-1938. The sheet gives the outline, '2' storeys, the brick, the label GARAGE, the alley wall on the alley line, the north wall on the 2013/2017 lot line (row 516.15 west of the building) with the key's fire-wall ticks on the alley line at its end and 2013's stable 0.62 m north of it, the south wall on the 2017/2021 lot line (row 598.11 west of it) with 2021's building 0.56 m south of it, one of the key's window marks on the alley wall (a cross with a dot for each storey) 7.38 m from the north wall, and a solid dot inside the south-east corner. The alley is on the EAST, so the kit is turned to face it (alley_side east) and built in mirror image (mirror), as 1612's stable is (T-1932), so that its party wall stands on the north lot line, where the sheet draws the fire-wall sign, and the open gable is the south end. That gable faces 2021's building across 0.56 m, so it carries no opening. On the alley wall, counted from the north party wall's inner face, laid out for its 15.2 m as 1900's 15.4 m stable is: a carriage bay 3.0 m clear under the loft hatch and hoist, a man door with a loft sash over it, the mark as a stable sash with a loft sash over it, a second carriage bay with a loft sash over it, and a stable sash and loft sash toward the south end. On the yard wall, counted from the gable end: three stable sash with loft sash over them and a door with a loft sash over it, the door where the walk to the house meets the yard wall. The workyard is the kit's: a brick apron 2.4 m wide along the yard wall and a walk to the house's rear wall line 10.56 m west (column 1056.93). The roof is the kit's gable with the ridge along the alley at its own 40 degrees, as 1900's 9.2 m deep stable takes, 4.46 m from eave to ridge over the 10.63 m span; no dormer and no ventilator, as the sheet draws none. No ramp, stair, lean-to, wing or range: the sheet draws none.

coach_house.note: The building's dimensions are the footprint's (inferred, above); its openings, roof and loft are the kit's, laid out for this lot, and RECONSTRUCTED. See the value's own note for each choice and what bounds it.

function.note: Sheet 35 of the 1911 Sanborn draws a two-storey brick building on the alley behind 2017, uncrossed, and letters it GARAGE. GARAGE is the 1911 sheet's word and is not read as the 1904 use (the K12 kit's restriction no_1911_use_labels; T-1837 study ruling 11; the T-1842 census row s35-2017-rear, whose own note backcasts the envelope and reconstructs the use as a stable/coach house). This record builds it as the house's stable and coach house: two carriage bays, a loft with its hatch and hoist, stable sash, and no motor-garage part. The use is RECONSTRUCTED; no source read names a horse, a carriage or a motor car on this lot.

citations.citation: Sanborn Map Company. Insurance Maps of Chicago, Illinois, Volume 3. New York: Sanborn Map Company, 1911. Sheet 35.

Architecture above the footprint beyond its story count, material colour and roof symbol

research_note: T-1938 refines the district draft (T-2352) in place under the same id onto the K12 coach-house kit, the fifth of the package's alley buildings on the east side of Prairie Avenue, 20th to 22nd Street, to leave the draft. The sheet census (census row s35-2017-rear, trace s35fp-2017-b2) carries the building into 1904; the draft rules now skip that row. Read afresh off the committed sheet 35 raster by median darkness profiles rather than taken from the draft's fitted rectangle (9.0 x 13.5 m): the sheet draws a building 10.63 m deep from the alley line and 15.23 m along it, the longest on this alley, standing on both of its lot lines, a fire-wall sign at its north end and a window mark on its alley wall. This copy of the sheet is coarse (0.186 m a pixel), so every reading here carries about a pixel. Nothing read dates the building before the 1911 sheet; that it stood by 1904 is the census's carry-back, which the district draft already made. No picture of the alley behind the 2000 block is known to this project.
